lines.text: Do you know how a bank vault keeps thieves out? It's not just a thick door. It's time.
A vault door can be over half a metre of steel and concrete, and weigh tens of tonnes, yet it swings on a hinge so balanced one person can push it.
When it closes, thick steel bolts slide out on every side, into the frame.
Then the time lock. Once set, the door can't open until a chosen time, like nine the next morning. Not even the manager can open it early.
If someone drills or tries to force it, a hidden relocker snaps more bolts into place.
Every layer just buys time, so alarms ring and help arrives before anyone gets through.
Orbi locks files too. A locked file needs its passcode, and after twelve wrong tries, it locks for good.
